newsitem.title: UK: Reuters behind EBS in Q1 forex deals - FT.
newsitem.headline: Reuters behind EBS in Q1 forex deals - FT.

text.p: Reuters Holdings Plc recorded fewer transactions on its electronic foreign exchange dealing system in the first quarter than rival system EBS, owned by a consortium of foreign exchange banks, the Financial Times reported on Monday.
The FT said the figures, from a Reuters document, showed a daily average of 21,000 deals on the Reuters Dealing 2000-2 system compared with 24,000 on EBS.

"There is room for two systems," a Reuters spokesman said in response to the article. "Reuters' strength lies in its subscriber base of over 1,200 banks, the number of countries and currencies, and its strength in certain currencies such as sterling," he added.
The FT said Reuters acknowledged that the number of EBS deals was bigger than the number of deals on its own system. EBS is seen as strong in major currency deals such as dollar/mark.
The FT noted that Reuters does not publicly reveal 2000-2 data, but said the Reuters document showed that the number of daily matches on its system had tripled since the start of 1995.
Reuters shares were down five pence at 635 by 0845 GMT.
